name: Power Window
description: Driver operates window switch to raise or lower the front left power window via LIN and CAN communication chain.
physicalOutput: Window motor drives glass to target position

interviewQuestions: Walk through the complete power window signal flow from switch to motor.
Why does the Door ECU use LIN instead of CAN?
How does anti-pinch work in power windows?
What happens if BCM loses communication with Door ECU?
Explain the AUTOSAR stack involved in window control.

oemNotes.Bosch: Bosch BCM implements WindowControl SWC with ASIL-B anti-pinch on AURIX TC3xx.
oemNotes.Continental: Continental door modules use LIN slave with Brose motor regulators.
oemNotes.Mercedes: Mercedes S-Class uses 4 independent LIN buses for door modules with centralized BCM.
oemNotes.Aptiv: Aptiv Smart Door concept integrates window, lock, and mirror on single LIN node.
oemNotes.ZF: ZF supplies gateway routing for cross-domain window commands.

knowledge.realVehicleExample: Ford F-150: Driver presses window switch → Brose Door ECU (LIN slave) → BCM (LIN master) → Gateway → CAN 0x245 → Door ECU motor driver → Brose regulator motor.
knowledge.vectorTool: CANoe with LIN option for full bus trace
knowledge.etasTool: RTA-CAR for AUTOSAR stack integration testing

steps.title: Driver Presses Power Window Switch
steps.beginnerExplanation: You press the window switch on the door panel — up to raise the window, down to lower it. This is the very first step of the entire process.
steps.engineeringExplanation: Mechanical momentary switch on door panel generates contact closure. Switch is wired to Door ECU ADC input or LIN switch matrix. Debounce filter applied in software.

steps.title: Door Switch Reads Voltage
steps.beginnerExplanation: The switch converts your press into an electrical signal that the door's small computer can understand.
steps.engineeringExplanation: Door ECU ADC reads switch voltage: UP=3.3V, DOWN=1.65V, NEUTRAL=0V. Software debounce timer (50ms) filters contact bounce before accepting state change.

steps.title: Door ECU Receives Signal
steps.beginnerExplanation: The Door ECU — a small computer inside the door — receives the switch signal and prepares to send it to the main body computer.
steps.engineeringExplanation: DoorControl SWC runnable triggered by switch state change event. SWC validates switch state, checks anti-pinch status, and prepares LIN response frame with switch position.

steps.title: AUTOSAR SWC Executes
steps.beginnerExplanation: The application software — like an app on the ECU — processes your request and decides what command to send.
steps.engineeringExplanation: WindowControl SWC in Door ECU executes: reads switch port, validates request against anti-pinch state, writes window command to sender port via RTE.

steps.title: RTE Routes Signal
steps.beginnerExplanation: RTE acts like a messenger, carrying your window request from the application software to the communication layer.
steps.engineeringExplanation: RTE_Write_WindowCmd() maps sender port data to LinIf transmit request. RTE generation from ARXML ensures type-safe port communication.

steps.title: LIN Frame Transmitted
steps.beginnerExplanation: The signal travels on the LIN bus — a simple single wire connecting the door to the main body computer.
steps.engineeringExplanation: LinIf transmits frame 0x3A on LIN schedule table slot at 19.2 kbps. Frame contains 8 bytes: switch state, position feedback, diagnostic status.

steps.title: BCM Receives LIN Frame
steps.beginnerExplanation: The BCM (Body Control Module) — the main body computer — receives the window request from the door via LIN.
steps.engineeringExplanation: BCM LinIf slave handler receives frame 0x3A, LinIf indication to PduR, COM unpacks DoorSwitch_State signal, RTE delivers to WindowControl SWC receiver port.

steps.title: COM Packs CAN PDU
steps.beginnerExplanation: COM packages the window command into a CAN message format ready for transmission on the vehicle's main network.
steps.engineeringExplanation: BCM WindowControl SWC writes WindowCmd signal. COM packs: byte0=position(0-100%), byte1=direction(UP/DOWN), byte2=anti-pinch enable into PDU 0x245.

steps.title: PduR Routes to CanIf
steps.beginnerExplanation: PduR routes the packaged message to the CAN interface for transmission on the vehicle network.
steps.engineeringExplanation: PduR routing path: COM PDU ID 0x245 → CanIf HTH 3 on CAN controller 0. PduR_Transmit() called with PDU info structure.

steps.title: CanIf Maps to CAN ID
steps.beginnerExplanation: CanIf assigns the correct CAN address (ID) to the message so the right ECU receives it.
steps.engineeringExplanation: CanIf maps PDU to HTH 3, sets CAN ID 0x245, DLC 8, calls CanDrv_Write() with hardware object handle.

steps.title: CAN Driver Transmits Frame
steps.beginnerExplanation: The CAN driver sends the electrical signal to the CAN controller chip inside the ECU.
steps.engineeringExplanation: CanDrv writes frame to CAN controller TX mailbox. Controller performs bit stuffing, CRC calculation, and arbitration on CAN_H/CAN_L differential pair.

steps.title: MCAL Configures Controller
steps.beginnerExplanation: MCAL sets up the hardware registers in the CAN controller chip to enable transmission.
steps.engineeringExplanation: MCAL Can driver configures TX mailbox registers, enables transmitter, sets baud rate timing segments (BS1, BS2, SJW) for 500kbps.

steps.title: CAN Bus Propagation
steps.beginnerExplanation: The message travels along the CAN bus wires at 500,000 bits per second to all ECUs on the network.
steps.engineeringExplanation: Differential signal on CAN_H (+2.5V) and CAN_L (+0.5V) propagates at ~5m/s along twisted pair. All bus participants receive frame. Arbitration ensures no collision.

steps.title: Gateway Routes Message
steps.beginnerExplanation: The Gateway ECU receives the message and forwards it to the correct network domain.
steps.engineeringExplanation: Gateway PduR receives CAN 0x245 on body CAN, routing table forwards to same bus (local) or cross-domain. SecOC verification if configured.

steps.title: Door ECU Receives CAN Frame
steps.beginnerExplanation: The Door ECU receives the window command from the CAN bus and prepares to drive the motor.
steps.engineeringExplanation: Door ECU CanIf HRH matches CAN ID 0x245, PduR indication to COM, signal unpacked, RTE delivers to MotorControl SWC receiver port.

steps.title: AUTOSAR Stack Processes Command
steps.beginnerExplanation: The full AUTOSAR software stack processes the command through all layers from application to hardware driver.
steps.engineeringExplanation: MotorControl SWC → RTE → (local processing) → MCAL PWM configuration. Anti-pinch algorithm monitors current during motor drive.

steps.title: Motor Driver Activated
steps.beginnerExplanation: The motor driver circuit amplifies the signal to provide enough power to move the window motor.
steps.engineeringExplanation: H-bridge driver IC enabled: IN1=HIGH, IN2=LOW for UP direction. PWM duty cycle set to 80% for smooth acceleration ramp over 200ms.

steps.title: Power Window Motor Drives
steps.beginnerExplanation: The 12V DC motor spins, driving the window regulator mechanism that physically moves the glass.
steps.engineeringExplanation: 12V DC motor draws 3-6A through H-bridge. Hall sensor provides position feedback at 100Hz. Anti-pinch monitors current — if >8A, motor reverses.

steps.title: Glass Moves to Position
steps.beginnerExplanation: The window glass moves up or down to the requested position. You can see and hear the window moving!
steps.engineeringExplanation: Window travels at ~15 cm/s. Position feedback via Hall sensor updates Door ECU every 10ms. Motor stops when target position reached or anti-pinch triggered. Position stored in NvM.
